props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer: a person is obligated to eat fourteen meals in the sukkah, one by day and one by night
the Sages: the matter has no fixed quota
the Sages: except the night of the first festival day alone [when eating in the sukkah is obligatory]
R' Eliezer further: one who did not eat on the first festival night compensates on the last festival night
the Sages: the matter has no compensation
and of this it is said: 'the crooked cannot be made straight, and the lacking cannot be counted' (Kohelet 1:15)
R' Eliezer's reason is the verse 'in sukkot you shall dwell (תשבו)'
'you shall dwell' -- in the manner that you reside: the sukkah is like one's dwelling
as in a dwelling [one eats] once by day and once by night, so in the sukkah once by day and once by night
and the Sages [what do they do with תשבו]? -- like a dwelling
the Sages' criterion: the sukkah is like a dwelling
as in a dwelling, if he wishes he eats and if not he does not, so in the sukkah too
R' Yochanan (in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name): so here [Sukkot] the first night is obligatory, from then on optional
as there [the festival of matzot] the first night is obligatory, from then on optional
and there, from where do we know? the verse says 'in the evening you shall eat matzot' (Shemot 12:18) -- Scripture fixed it as an obligation
